nodes.label: Native App Icon (Avantej)
nodes.description: Primary app icon for the Avantej Expo/React Native mobile app. Displays a stylized 3D glossy letter 'A' in blue gradient (light to dark blue) centered on a pale/light blue background. Design overlays include golden-ratio/composition guide circles and crosshair lines (dashed blue), consistent with Expo icon design tooling. The 'A' letterform has rounded tube-like arms meeting at a peak, no crossbar — an angular boomerang/chevron shape. Used as the launcher icon for the member-facing native app.

nodes.label: Logo-B (Native App Brand Asset)
nodes.description: Avantej brand logo variant B for the React Native / Expo mobile app. The mark is a stylized fingerprint rendered in solid black on a white/transparent background. Concentric oval ridges spiral inward, terminating in a central letterform that reads as a combined 'A' or abstract 'C/O' — consistent with 'Avantej' initial identity. The fingerprint motif evokes identity, uniqueness, and biometric/security themes appropriate for a multi-tenant SaaS platform managing member access and permissions. Monochrome palette (pure black strokes, white fill) makes it suitable for both light-mode UI and dark-background overlays. The design is icon-grade: no wordmark is included, making it suitable as an app icon, splash-screen mark, or tab-bar logo.

nodes.label: ADR 0001: Direct Charges on Stripe Connect for Customer→Tenant Payments
nodes.contributor: rationale: Direct charges chosen so statement descriptor matches Tenant brand, dispute/refund burden stays with Tenant, GST liability stays with Tenant. Destination charges and separate-charges+transfers rejected because they make Avantej merchant of record for services it does not operate.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: direct charges on stripe connect for customer→tenant payments

nodes.label: ADR 0002: Hybrid Monetization — SaaS Base Subscription + Per-Transaction Application Fee
nodes.contributor: rationale: Hybrid (Model C) provides revenue floor from SaaS sub + upside from app fee (2% one-time, 1% recurring). Sub-only leaves upside on table; per-txn-only has no floor; tiered with overage deferred to v2.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: hybrid monetization — saas base subscription + per-transaction application fee

nodes.label: ADR 0003: Parallel Trial With Independent SaaS and Connect Gates
nodes.contributor: rationale: Low signup friction — Tenants explore for 14-day trial before being forced to subscribe. Connect onboarding only required when enabling customer payments, not for internal features. Sub-first and Connect-first alternatives rejected for high friction.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003: parallel trial with independent saas and connect gates

nodes.label: ADR 0004: v1 Payment Scope (Phases 0,1,2,3,6-lite,7)
nodes.contributor: rationale: v1 includes SaaS billing, Connect onboarding, one-time package purchase, ledger mirror, webhook idempotency. Deferred: recurring memberships, trainer split, audit UI, multi-currency, refund UI, Stripe Tax. Full scope rejected as taking 5-6 weeks vs 3.5 for first pilot.

nodes.label: ADR 0005: Stripe Customer Mapping in Tenant DB
nodes.contributor: rationale: Stripe Customer objects are per-connected-account; a user buying from two Tenants needs two Stripe Customers. Mapping stored in tenant DB to avoid cross-DB writes during payment flows. Control-panel table rejected as it couples billing transactions to control-plane.

nodes.label: ADR 0006: Webhook Architecture and Idempotency
nodes.contributor: rationale: Split endpoints /webhooks/stripe/platform and /webhooks/stripe/connect allow independent secret rotation. Dedupe table in control-panel DB (processed_webhook_events) provides cross-cutting idempotency. Synchronous v1 handlers — async queue deferred. Single endpoint rejected (shared secret), pure natural-key idempotency rejected (not all events have clean keys).

nodes.label: ADR 0007: Customer Payment UX — Stripe PaymentSheet (RN SDK) with Server-Side Finalization
nodes.rationale: Use Stripe PaymentSheet from @stripe/stripe-react-native for card collection. Server creates PaymentIntent on the tenant's connected account; finalization (package_instance creation, ledger mirror) happens in the payment_intent.succeeded webhook, not on client return. UUID idempotency key prevents double-charges. Done page polls for webhook materialization.

Custom UI with CardField (higher cost, no UX win)
Client-side finalization (unreliable on disconnect)

nodes.label: ADR 0008: Tenant Connect Onboarding via Embedded Components on Web
nodes.rationale: Use embedded <ConnectAccountOnboarding> component on web for tenant Stripe Connect KYC/onboarding in v1. Tenants stay on Avantej domain. Server endpoints: connect.getOrCreateAccount (idempotent Express account creation), connect.createAccountSession (returns client_secret for component), connect.dashboardLink (fallback). Organizations table gains stripeConnectStatus, chargesEnabled, payoutsEnabled, detailsSubmitted columns synced via account.updated webhook.
alternatives_rejected: Hosted account link redirect (breaks brand presence)
Custom UI on Accounts API (high maintenance)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008: tenant connect onboarding via embedded components on web

nodes.label: ADR 0009: SaaS Subscription Past-Due Behavior and Dunning
nodes.rationale: 7-day grace period from past_due. State machine: active/trialing=full access; past_due within grace=full+banner; past_due past grace=read-only (SAAS_PAST_DUE_READONLY); unpaid/canceled=read-only; incomplete=blocked entirely. Connect payment path NOT gated on SaaS sub state — end customers can still purchase. Stripe built-in dunning emails for v1. pastDueAt and gracePeriodEndsAt columns added to subscriptions.
alternatives_rejected: Hard cut Connect on past_due (harms end customers)
Penalty app-fee on past_due (adds dynamic-fee complexity)
3-day grace (too aggressive)
14-day grace (too lenient)
Custom Avantej dunning emails (deferred to v2)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009: saas subscription past-due behavior and dunning

nodes.label: ADR 0010: SaaS Tier Shape — Hybrid Quantitative Limits + Feature Flags
nodes.rationale: Hybrid model: each tier (Basic/Professional/Enterprise) defines both quantitative resource limits (orgs, locations, members, customers, monthlyTxns) and binary feature flags (ghl, commissionSplits, memberships, apiAccess). Single source of truth in packages/types/src/tiers.ts TIER_LIMITS. Application fee is tier-driven (3%/2%/1.5%) stored as applicationFeeBps. Feature gates: requireTierFeature middleware (TIER_FEATURE_LOCKED). Quant limits: assertWithinLimit at write time (TIER_LIMIT_REACHED). Soft cap on downgrade.
alternatives_rejected: Pure quantitative limits (inflexible for capability features)
Pure feature flags (loses upsell for high-volume tenants)
Defer tier enforcement to v2 (pricing page lacks credibility)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010: saas tier shape — hybrid quantitative limits + feature flags

nodes.label: ADR 0011: Reconciliation Strategy — Nightly Cron with Handler Replay
nodes.rationale: Webhooks remain primary; nightly cron (03:00 UTC via CF Cron) is safety net. Scope: platform Subscription list, per-tenant PaymentIntent.list (48h window), per-tenant Account.retrieve. Repair mechanism: same handler functions used by webhooks, Stripe object fetched directly (bypassing webhook signature). processed_webhook_events.source distinguishes 'reconciler' from 'platform'/'connect'. Manual trigger via admin.reconcileNow oRPC procedure.
alternatives_rejected: Pull-only periodic sync (higher API volume, lower freshness)
On-demand reconcile only (issues invisible)
Reconcile via direct DB writes bypassing handlers (two code paths)
Hourly reconcile (higher API cost, no meaningful freshness gain)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0011: reconciliation strategy — nightly cron with handler replay

nodes.label: ADR 0012: Dev Sandbox Topology and v1 Launch Currency
nodes.rationale: Single Avantej Stripe account with four named sandboxes: default-test (manual exploration), dev-shared (all engineers + preview deploys), ci-e2e (GitHub Actions), staging (pre-prod). Per-dev sandboxes rejected (5-cap doesn't scale). v1 ships USD-only. Schema-forward: every monetary table carries currency text column from day one. Amounts in integer minor units (cents). Application-fee math uses integer arithmetic only.
alternatives_rejected: Per-developer sandbox (rejected due to 5-cap)
Multi-currency in v1 (rejected for timeline)
Single sandbox for dev+CI+staging (cross-pollution)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0012: dev sandbox topology and v1 launch currency

nodes.label: ADR 0013: Payment Side Effects on payment_intent.succeeded
nodes.rationale: Implement post-payment side effects as a separate service payment-side-effects.service.ts called synchronously from the connect webhook handler. Each side effect is independently try/caught. V1 scope: (1) flip appointments.status pending→confirmed, (2) append appointment_status_history row (actor=system, reason=payment_confirmed), (3) send receipt email via Resend (members→auth.user.email; walk-ins→walk_in_customers.email). A side-effect throw must never reach the webhook ack path.
alternatives_rejected: Inline in webhook handler (couples handler to side-effect, bloats handler)
Queue-driven runner (v1 simplicity; revisit if side effects exceed 5 or latency causes Stripe retries)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013: payment side effects on payment_intent.succeeded

nodes.label: ADR 0014: Refund Stripe Account via Snapshot, Not Resolver
nodes.rationale: Snapshot the Stripe Connect account ID on the payment row at charge time (stripe_connect_account_id_snapshot column). At refund time, use the snapshot, never the country resolver. Columns: appointments.stripe_connect_account_id_snapshot, payments.stripe_connect_account_id_snapshot, customer_profiles.stripe_connect_account_id_snapshot. Stripe handles fee reversal automatically via refund_application_fee:true so no fee% calc needed. Same pattern for saved-card charges.
alternatives_rejected: Re-resolve at refund time via country resolver (race after tenant restructuring)
Store only PaymentIntent id, look up via Stripe API (extra API call + network failure point)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014: refund stripe account via snapshot, not resolver

nodes.label: ADR 0015: Package Purchase via Stripe Payment Link
nodes.rationale: Use Stripe Payment Link for package purchases. Flow: create package_instances row (status=pending), create Stripe Price on tenant's Connect acct, create Payment Link with application_fee_amount and metadata (type:package, packageInstanceId, organizationId). payment_intent_data.metadata must mirror Payment Link metadata explicitly for webhook event to carry packageInstanceId. Webhook fast path on payment_intent.succeeded flips package to paid/active. UI surfaces URL with Copy/SMS/WhatsApp share buttons.
alternatives_rejected: Stripe Checkout via redirect (equivalent but more code)
Stripe Elements in-app (card-present only, no remote)
Manual reconciliation (shifts burden to staff)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: package purchase via stripe payment link

nodes.label: ADR 0016: Card-on-File via SetupIntent + Off-Session Charges
nodes.rationale: Card-on-file via standard Stripe pattern: (1) get-or-create Stripe Customer on tenant's Connect acct with metadata; (2) save card via SetupIntent usage=off_session, web mounts Elements+PaymentElement, confirms; (3) list saved cards from snapshot acct; (4) charge saved card off-session using customer's snapshot acct (not country resolver). SCA requires_action surfaces as toast in v1 — manual follow-up. Stripe Customer per tenant scope (tenant owns customer relationship).
alternatives_rejected: Stripe Subscriptions for memberships (pricing patterns not Stripe-friendly in v1)
Customer on platform acct (violates merchant-of-record boundary, Stripe classification problem)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0016: card-on-file via setupintent + off-session charges

nodes.label: ADR 0017: Per-Country Stripe Connect Accounts
nodes.rationale: Introduce org_country_stripe_accounts table (organization_id, country_code, stripe_account_id, currency, charges_enabled, payouts_enabled, details_submitted, status). Resolution at charge time: appointment.branch_id → hierarchy_nodes.country_node_id → country name → ISO code → getConnectAccountForOrgCountry. Falls back to legacy organizations.stripe_connect_account_id. OAuth state encodes countryCode as 4-part HMAC payload. UI: multi-country list at /billing/connect. Legacy column preserved for 1-release deprecation.
alternatives_rejected: One global Stripe acct + auto-FX (~2% FX fee, country restrictions)
Per-branch acct (too granular; branches in same country share legal entity)
Defer to product market expansion (schema cost small now, migration later expensive)

nodes.label: ADR 0018: Platform Payment Ledger as Audit Mirror
nodes.rationale: Use existing platform_payment_ledger control-panel table as write-only audit mirror, idempotent on stripe_event_id. Event kinds: pi_succeeded, pi_refunded, saas_invoice_paid, application_fee_collected. Key fields: stripe_event_id (UNIQUE dedupe), organization_id (nullable), event_kind, stripe_object_id, stripe_account, amount/application_fee/currency (minor units), occurred_at (Stripe time). INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Writes from webhook handlers (real-time) and C.1 backfill cron.
alternatives_rejected: Query Stripe live every time (rate-limited, slow, breaks on outage)
Per-tenant rows in tenant DB (cross-tenant aggregation requires fan-out)
Event-sourcing full Stripe payload as JSONB (columnar aggregation wins over blob)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0018: platform payment ledger as audit mirror

nodes.label: ADR 0019: Reconciliation Policy
nodes.rationale: Resources: Payments + Refunds + Application fees (Payouts deferred). Drift policy: alert-only in v1, no auto-fix. Drift rows inserted into payment_drift_log with severity, surfaced in platform-admin UI. Lookback: checkpoint + 24h buffer; per-(org, country, resource_type) row in reconciliation_state stores last_reconciled_at. Severity tiered: missing_in_db <10min=info, >=10min=critical; amount_mismatch/currency_mismatch=critical.
alternatives_rejected: Auto-fix for safe drift kinds (buggy reconciler = silent corruption at scale)
Hourly reconciliation (API rate limits, scale fine with nightly)
Replay via stripe.events.list (that is C.1's role; reconciliation is resource-state check)

nodes.label: ADR 0020: Dispute Handling Workflow
nodes.rationale: Triple-delivery on every dispute event (charge.dispute.created/updated/closed/funds_reinstated/funds_withdrawn): (1) tenant email via Resend to org owner (informational events skip email), (2) tenant in-app notification row in tenant DB, (3) platform admin queue UPSERT in control-panel platform_dispute_queue keyed on dispute_id. Each side effect independently try/caught. Webhook handler always returns 200. Evidence submission stays in Stripe Dashboard for v1.
alternatives_rejected: Single-channel notification (payment incidents too important)
In-app evidence submission UI (high effort, Stripe Dashboard already production-grade)
Dispute row per event (admins want current state, not event history)
Slack alerting (deferred to future Plan C v2)

nodes.label: ADR 0021: Cloudflare Workers Cron as Scheduled-Job Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Use CF Cron Triggers + scheduled handler dispatching to oRPC service functions. Crons declared in wrangler.jsonc: 0 * * * * (C.1 webhook backfill), 30 2 * * * (C.5 reconciliation), 0 9 * * * (C.6 onboarding-stuck alert). Work runs inside ctx.waitUntil. Lazy imports per cron to keep cold-start cost off the fetch path. Manual triggers call the same service function from an oRPC handler — identical code path.
alternatives_rejected: External cron (separate deploy dependency, service-key auth, schedule in different config)
Durable Object alarms (wrong shape for platform-scoped crons; DO is per-tenant shape)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0021: cloudflare workers cron as scheduled-job infrastructure

nodes.label: ADR 0022: Tenant Management Surface Scope
nodes.rationale: Plan E is platform-admin-only. Every endpoint gated behind requirePlatformAdmin() under /dashboard/platform-admin/* route prefix. Self-serve tenant management (owner-facing subscription management, own-tenant audit history, own-tenant data export, in-app cancellation) deferred to Plan F. Admin-mediated GDPR export within 30 days is compliant.
alternatives_rejected: Build platform-admin and tenant self-serve in parallel (doubles work)
Tenant-only Plan E (operationally can't run SaaS without admin surface)
Build admin surface but expose subset to tenants via RBAC (auth-model branching + security risk)

nodes.label: ADR 0023: Tenant Usage Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Daily cron at 01:00 UTC writes tenant_usage_snapshots with bounded concurrency (=5) cross-DB fan-out. Counters per tenant per day: member_count, customer_count, appt_count_30d, sales_total_30d_minor, sales_currency, storage_bytes (deferred), ghl_active. UPSERT on (organization_id, snapshot_date) for idempotency. Manual trigger runTenantUsageSnapshotsNow on admin router. Admin UI reads from control-panel only — no fan-out at request time.
alternatives_rejected: Realtime streaming (hot-path side effect on every business write)
On-demand fan-out with KV cache (first uncached request pays fan-out; no history)
Snapshot every N hours (hourly multiplies rows 24x for no business signal)

nodes.label: ADR 0024: Tenant Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: organizations.paymentStatus is the authoritative lifecycle state. States: created→trial→active↔past_due→suspended→cancelled→deleted. Suspend semantics: block charges + block app login (middleware returns 403 for suspended/cancelled). Platform-admin bypass. forceCancelTenant: calls stripe.subscriptions.cancel(), sets paymentStatus='cancelled', audits. issueTenantCredit: adds negative customer balance in Stripe for next invoice. reTrialTenant: extends trialEndsAt, sets paymentStatus='active', does NOT modify Stripe sub.
alternatives_rejected: Stripe as source of truth (every gate check requires Stripe API call)
Half-suspend block charges only (tenant staff books appointments customers can't pay)
Hard delete on cancel (legal hold, dispute, refund needs data)

nodes.label: ADR 0025: Activation Funnel Milestone Definitions
nodes.rationale: Seven milestones in logical operational sequence: (1) email_verified, (2) hierarchy_seeded, (3) first_member, (4) first_customer, (5) ghl_connected, (6) first_appointment, (7) first_payment. Each milestone's reachedAt = MIN(created_at) of qualifying row. stuckAt = first unreached milestone. No new persistence — derived from existing tables at read time. Five parallel tenant-DB count queries per drill-in.
alternatives_rejected: Event-sourced milestones / tenant_events log (new persistence coupled to every business write)
Compute funnel during daily usage snapshot (doubles cron work, column-bloat risk)
5 or 9 milestones (7 is the natural onboarding sequence)

nodes.label: ADR 0026: Tenant Deletion & GDPR Workflow
nodes.rationale: Two-stage delete: (1) soft delete — write tenant_deletions row with hard_delete_after=now+30d, set paymentStatus='cancelled'; (2) hard delete — daily cron sweeper at 0 3 * * * drops Neon project and deletes organizations row. Restore: super_admin stamps restored_at within 30 days, flips paymentStatus='active'. Export: JSON dump per tenant table, base64-encoded, stored in tenant_deletions.export_url (stop-gap; R2 upgrade required at scale). Neon project DELETE is synchronous and irreversible.
alternatives_rejected: Immediate hard delete (foot-cannon on misclick)
Forever-soft-delete (not GDPR compliant)
CSV-per-table export (Cloudflare Workers no built-in ZIP encoder)

nodes.label: ADR 0027: Plan F Scope (Platform-Admin Only)
nodes.rationale: Plan F is platform-admin-only operational UX layer on top of Plan E. Scope: F.1 (⌘K cross-tenant search, Notes tab, Tags+bulk ops), F.2 (/revenue MRR/ARR/churn, /comms outbox+template library), F.3 (Billing tab, invoice history, refund, tier change, coupons), F.4 (/renewals, /health, /webhooks log, /migrations runner). Out of scope: tenant self-serve management, self-serve signup, cross-tenant analytics, referral program, hard quota enforcement, per-tenant Neon region migration, in-app dispute response, Slack alerts. All routes under /dashboard/platform-admin/*.
alternatives_rejected: Single mega-phase (too long for one PR review)
Mix tenant-side surfaces into Plan F (ADR-0022 decides self-serve is separate)
Build tags as jsonb on organizations (see ADR-0029)

nodes.label: ADR 0028: Tenant Notes as Soft-State, Append-Only Audit
nodes.rationale: Dedicated tenant_notes table (id, organization_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, author_user_id text, body, is_pinned, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). Partial indexes on (org, created_at DESC) and (org, is_pinned, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. Edit window: 1 hour by note author, then frozen; super_admin can soft-delete any time. Every create/update/delete writes platform-admin audit log row. 1h edit window relies on server clock (UTC, no client-clock injection risk).
alternatives_rejected: Per-org jsonb array (not indexable, no per-row audit, no soft delete, volume bloat)
Unlimited edit audit-log-everything (noisy or fragile on debounced UPDATEs)
Per-note edit history table (overkill for 1h window)
nodes.norm_label: adr 0028: tenant notes as soft-state, append-only audit
